name: Murrah ibn Hammam
bio: Murrah ibn Hammam was of Dhuhl ibn Shaiban, a branch of Bakr ibn Wa'il long settled in al-'Iraq, near the royal house of al-Hirah. Lyall has no information to fix the date of his short poem.
It concerns a raid on his herd of camels by a man named 'Auf.

poems.title: Ode LXXXII: O my two comrades, saddle the
poems.author: Murrah ibn Hammam
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Murrah son of Hammam, of Dhuhl ibn Shaiban, of Bakr ibn Wa'il.
poems.text:
O my two comrades, saddle the camels and hasten : for verily the time has come for the starter on his way to feel heart's pain !

Long has been the stay here : so bring near to me a full-grown she-camel, strong and sturdy, fit to carry two through the desert lands.

She has eaten of the barley of as-Sailahun and its clover, and out of it she has stored up for me fleetness ;

And she is like a she-ostrich in the sand-margin of Mulaihah, with her legs dyed green with the herbage, tall, vying in speed with a black-plumaged male.

O 'Auf, woe to thee ! what has emboldened thee to take possession of my troop of camels ? It was my custom from long ago to send them forth to feed far afield in thy direction.

By God ! were it not that the folk who owned them were all scattered far and wide — and the worst of things that a man can say is a lie ! —

I had sent in the direction of the cry for help the rushing of a multitude (?), and I had mounted a short-haired steed, spare and lithe like a palm-branch stripped of its leaves ;

And ye should have left my camels feeding peacefully — for I am one of those who drive away from my herds a host disappointed of their booty.

A goodly warrior is 'Auf when he clothes himself in his armour : and woe is me, the yoke-fellow of defeat !
